verses.text: In the seventeenth year of the reign of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. Unlike his ancestor David, he didn't do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel. He even made his son pass through the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
He offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up to wage war against Jerusalem. They laid siege to Ahaz but couldn't defeat him.
At that time King Rezin of Syria took Elath back for Syria and drove the people of Judah out. Syrians moved into Elath, and they live there to this day.
Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria with this message: “I am your servant and your son. Come rescue me from the kings of Syria and Israel who are attacking me.”
Ahaz took the silver and gold from the LORD's house and the palace treasuries and sent it to the king of Assyria as a gift.
The king of Assyria listened. He attacked Damascus and captured it, took its people captive to Kir, and killed Rezin.
King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria. He saw the altar there and sent Urijah the priest a drawing and detailed plans for it.
Urijah the priest built an altar according to the plans King Ahaz had sent from Damascus. He had it ready by the time the king came back.
When the king returned from Damascus and saw the altar, he went up to it and made an offering.
He burned his burnt offering and grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and splashed the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.
The bronze altar that stood before the LORD was between Ahaz's altar and the LORD's house. Ahaz moved it from the front of the house to the north side of his own altar.

King Ahaz told Urijah the priest, “Use the large altar for the morning burnt offering, the evening grain offering, my burnt offering and grain offering, and the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings of all the people. Splash all the blood from the burnt offerings and sacrifices on it. I'll use the bronze altar when I need to make an inquiry.”
Urijah the priest did everything King Ahaz had ordered.
King Ahaz cut the panels off the stands and removed the basins from them. He also took the Sea down from the bronze oxen underneath it and set it on a stone pavement.
Because of the king of Assyria, he removed the covered passage that had been built for the Sabbath and the king's outer entrance to the LORD's house.
The rest of Ahaz's acts and what he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Ahaz died and joined his ancestors. He was buried with them in David's City, and his son Hezekiah became king in his place.
